edges.description: Cutis laxa is present in all three of the 2017 patients and in the Chinese patient, and it recurs across the V-ATPase-related CDGs. Elastic-fibre assembly depends on secretory-pathway processing, which is what the pump defect disturbs, but no dermal or elastin measurement exists in any ATP6AP2 patient. edges.description: Mild intellectual disability in two of the 2017 patients. The neurological ATP6AP2 diseases are much more severe and are caused by a different allele class, so the cognitive phenotype here cannot simply be read as a mild version of those — and the 2026 finding of shared glycosylation abnormalities complicates it further rather than settling it.

edges.description: Liver-restricted deletion produces hypoglycosylation of serum proteins and autophagy defects, establishing that the liver is a sufficient source of the circulating glycosylation abnormality.
edges.limitations: It is a complete knockout where the patients carry missense alleles that retain protein — in one case at normal abundance — so the model tests loss of the gene rather than the patients' lesion. It is also liver-restricted and acutely induced in an adult animal, where the human disease is germline and developmental, so nothing in it speaks to the cutis laxa, the immunodeficiency or the cognitive phenotype.

edges.description: It is the only system in this literature in which lysosomal acidification itself is measured, which is the step the whole mechanism turns on.
edges.limitations: An invertebrate, and the fat body is a functional analogue of liver rather than liver. The substitution is introduced into the fly orthologue, so residue context and the ATP6AP1-equivalent interaction are not the human ones. Survival and lipid metabolism are organism-level readouts in a system whose life history has no counterpart in the human disease.

nodes.description:
Three missense alleles are published across three families, and all three fall in exon 3, in the extracellular domain of the protein: c.293T>C p.Leu98Ser de novo in the Portuguese patient, c.212G>A p.Arg71His in two brothers of a German family, and c.185G>A p.Gly62Glu in the Chinese patient. Neither of the first two appears in more than 60,000 ExAC controls.
The clustering matters. The neurological ATP6AP2 diseases are caused by splicing variants that reduce the amount of normal protein; this entity is caused by missense substitutions in one domain that impair what the protein does. Allele class, not gene, is what decides which disease a patient gets — and even that separation is less clean than it looks, since the 2026 work finds glycosylation abnormalities in splicing patients too.

nodes.description:
The V-ATPase is built in two sectors: the V0 proton pore, assembled in the endoplasmic reticulum under the control of a set of assembly factors, and the V1 ATP-hydrolysis domain, added in the Golgi. ATP6AP1 and ATP6AP2 are its two accessory subunits, and ATP6AP1 is the orthologue of the yeast V0 assembly factor Voa1.
So a variant that weakens the ATP6AP2-ATP6AP1 interaction is a variant that interferes with V0 assembly at its earliest step. That is the hinge of this disease: everything downstream follows from a pump that is not properly built, not from anything ATP6AP2 does on its own.

nodes.description:
Low immunoglobulins with a poor polysaccharide antibody response, decreased CD4 and increased CD8 lymphocytes in the Portuguese patient; IgG subclass deficiency with reduced IgG1 and IgG3 in one German brother; normal immunological status in the other.
How a V-ATPase accessory subunit defect produces an antibody deficiency is not established in this disease at all. The most this entry can say is that hypogammaglobulinaemia is a recurring feature of the V-ATPase-related CDGs — ATP6AP1 deficiency manifests with hypogammaglobulinaemia alongside liver and cognitive abnormalities — so it appears to be a property of the pump rather than of this subunit. Hence HYPOTHETICAL.

nodes.description:
The V-ATPase acidifies organelles of the secretory and endocytic pathway, and through that controls proteolytic processing, protein degradation, autophagy and glycosylation. With V0 assembly impaired, those compartments are insufficiently acidified.
Defective lysosomal acidification was demonstrated directly in the Drosophila fat body — the fly's liver-like tissue — carrying one of the patient substitutions. That is where this node stops being an inference from the biochemistry and becomes a measurement, albeit in an invertebrate.

nodes.description:
Performed in the Chinese patient at eleven months for cirrhosis with coagulopathy and anaemia. No outcome beyond the fact of the transplant is reported.
Two things follow that a reader should weigh. A transplant replaces the organ but not the genotype, so the immunological, dermatological and cognitive features remain; and the serum glycosylation defect would be expected to correct, since the mouse experiment shows the liver is a sufficient source of it — which would make transferrin a useless marker of disease activity post-transplant. Neither point is addressed in any published source, and neither is asserted here as more than the reading it is.

nodes.description: Adeno-Cre injection to delete Atp6ap2 in mouse liver, against adeno-GFP controls. It tests whether losing ATP6AP2 in the liver is sufficient for the serum phenotype, which is the question a patient series cannot answer.

All patient sera show an abnormal transferrin profile — decreased tetrasialotransferrin with increased tri-, di- and monosialotransferrin — and HPLC put the correctly glycosylated fraction at about half in two patients. It is a type II pattern, meaning the defect is in processing rather than in assembly of the glycan.
The magnitude is worth stating because it is modest, and because it is the finding that gets this disease its name while not being the finding that makes patients ill. Half-normal transferrin glycosylation does not explain micronodular cirrhosis at sixteen months.
